Every shell of the Sydney Opera House is cut from one sphere. 🌐 Watch it go up: 14 years in 31 seconds. ⏱️

The old tram depot on Bennelong Point came down in 1958 and the podium went up, before anyone knew how to build the roof. In 1961 came the breakthrough: make every shell a slice of the same sphere. Then 2,400 precast ribs, lifted rib by rib, and about 1.06 million Swedish tiles.

The twist: the architect, Jørn Utzon, quit in 1966 and never saw it finished. It opened in 1973, ten years late, at $102 million against a $7 million estimate.

Would you have kept going without the architect? Yes or no 👇

yt_description:
Construction began in March 1959 on Bennelong Point; the podium (1959–1963) went up before the roof was solved. In 1961 the 'spherical solution' made every shell a section of one sphere. Stage III (1963–1967): 2,400 precast ribs and 4,000 roof panels made on site, ~1.056 million Höganäs tiles. Utzon left in 1966; Queen Elizabeth II opened it on 20 Oct 1973, ten years late, at $102 M vs a $7 M estimate.

Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Opera_House · https://www.newworldencyclopedia.org/entry/Sydney_Opera_House
Figures are historical estimates. Animation is a stylised reconstruction.
